This high multiple suggests that investors are willing to pay a premium, possibly due to optimistic future growth expectations or other factors not reflected in the recent financials. Additionally, the compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -38% [E13], indicating a decline in profitability. This negative trend is concerning and implies potential risks for shareholders, as it suggests that the company has struggled to generate profits recently. The high P/E ratio combined with declining profitability raises questions about the sustainability of current valuations.
